title: Oven-Roasted Melting Argentinian Bean Flatbread
description: Sweet, molten flatbreads made with black beans and a double-rise dough for a low-calorie date-night treat.
instructions: In a large bowl whisk together whole wheat flour, all-purpose flour, salt, sugar, ground cumin, smoked paprika, dried oregano, and active dry yeast until well combined.
Add water, olive oil, and mashed black beans to the dry mixture, stirring until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead the dough on a lightly floured surface for about 5-7 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Place the dough in an oiled bowl, cover loosely, and let it rise at room temperature for 60 minutes until nearly doubled in size.
Punch down the dough, divide it into 4 equal portions, and roll each into a flat disc about 10 inches in diameter.
Place the discs on a parchment-lined baking sheet, cover again, and let them rise for a second time for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) while the dough is in its second rise.
Bake the flatbreads for 12 to 15 minutes until the edges blister and the surface has a golden crust.
Remove from the oven, let cool for 5 minutes, then slice and serve warm.
